cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You can borrow the dress for ten pounds and an acknowledgment that you mocked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Money covers fabric. It doesn't cover wearing my bad taste proudly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now say which part of my judgement improved since yesterday.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets ten pounds and acknowledgment of mockery; A3 rules double money cannot buy emotional repair; A5 demands explanation of changed judgment beyond B garment praise.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 twenty offer to distinguish fabric from insult; A5 uses B4 beautiful concession to demand recognition of A judgment.

relationship.evidence: B2 tries money and B4 concedes beauty, plausible borrower attempting to settle terms.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes B4 compliment insufficient because the deeper price concerns the person whose taste B mocked.

specificity.evidence: A1 borrowed dress price and prior mockery; B2 actual money offer; B4 praise make the transaction clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 judgment improved since yesterday is pointed irony tied to prior mockery, not a new unrelated grievance.

coach2.inferred: A5 implies B judgment changed rather than A taste objectively improved; irony is intelligible.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 offers twice A1 practical price.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 rejects B2 money as payment for the emotional debt.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 gives A3 desired dress praise.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 uses B4 praise to demand an account of changed view of A taste.
